about.heading: About Me (&) My Journey
about.intro: I got into SEO wanting to know why some sites grow without ad spend while others stay invisible. Three years and 30+ websites later, I am still chasing that answer.

cards.heading: Where the questions started
cards.short: BBA Marketing at IMSciences, Peshawar. The degree gave me the framework; search gave me the obsession.
cards.long: I studied BBA Marketing at IMSciences in Peshawar. Somewhere between coursework and curiosity I started asking why some websites pull traffic for free while others pay for every visitor and still stay invisible.

cards.heading: Measuring what people trust
cards.short: Final year research on consumer trust in e-commerce and how perceived risk shapes what people actually buy.
cards.long: My final year research looked at consumer trust in e-commerce and its effect on online purchasing behaviour, using the PROCESS macro and a Sobel test to measure perceived risk as a mediating variable. The same quantitative thinking still shapes how I read conversion behaviour and SEO performance.

cards.heading: First real audits
cards.short: Learning that most sites are not held back by content. They are held back by things nobody has looked at.
cards.long: Early audit work taught me the pattern that still holds: most websites are not underperforming because the writing is weak. They are underperforming because crawl paths are broken, titles are duplicated, and nobody has checked in months.

cards.heading: Technical foundations
cards.short: Crawl budgets, redirect chains, schema, indexation. The unglamorous work that decides everything else.
cards.long: I went deep on technical SEO because it is where the compounding happens. Speed issues, redirect chains and indexation gaps quietly cost rankings every single week, and none of it shows up in a content calendar.

cards.heading: Seven sites at once
cards.short: Google Ads & SEO Executive at DX Creativ. Seven live client sites, every one at a different stage.
cards.long: At DX Creativ I managed full SEO across seven live client websites simultaneously, spanning technical audits, on-page fixes, content strategy and link-building oversight, while running Google Ads search campaigns for lead generation alongside it.

cards.heading: Paid and organic as one system
cards.short: Performance Growth Marketer at Remote Opus. Ads and SEO stopped being two separate jobs.
cards.long: At Remote Opus I run performance marketing end to end: Google and Meta Ads, SEO, landing pages, and conversion tracking. Seeing which keywords convert in paid is the fastest way to sharpen the organic strategy, so I stopped treating them as separate disciplines.

cards.heading: The work continues
cards.short: Still auditing what is broken, fixing what matters most, and building around what buyers already search for.
cards.long: The approach has not changed: audit what is broken, fix what matters most, and build content and campaigns around what buyers are already searching for. Not templates, not guesswork.

items.q: How long before I see results?
items.a: Technical fixes can show movement in weeks; content and authority take months. Most projects show measurable change in Search Console within 6 to 12 weeks, with the larger gains compounding after that. Anyone promising page 1 in 30 days is selling something.

items.q: Do you work on paid ads as well as SEO?
items.a: Yes, and I prefer to run them together. Paid data tells you which keywords actually convert, which makes the organic strategy far sharper. Treating them as two separate jobs wastes the most useful signal you have.

items.q: What does an SEO audit actually cover?
items.a: A full crawl of the site, then technical, on-page and content review, plus keyword and competitor gap analysis. You get a prioritised fix list ordered by impact rather than by ease, and a call to walk through it.

items.q: Can you work with my existing site?
items.a: That is most of what I do. Whether it needs a technical cleanup, a content structure, schema, or a full migration handled without losing rankings, I can step into an existing build rather than starting over.

items.q: Which platforms have you worked with?
items.a: WordPress, Shopify, Magento and Strapi among others, across e-commerce, travel, B2B services and agency portfolios. The platform changes what is easy; it rarely changes what actually needs fixing.
Yes. Google Business Profile optimisation, local pack visibility, and the service and location pages that turn nearby searches into enquiries. It is often the fastest win for service businesses.

items.q: How do you report on progress?
items.a: Search Console and analytics data rather than screenshots of rankings. You see impressions, clicks, positions and conversions, plus what changed and what it moved. If something is not working I will tell you.

items.q: Not sure what your site needs?
items.a: Reach out and describe the situation. Most audits and strategy calls start within 48 hours, and you will get an honest read on what is holding the site back, with no sales pitch attached.
